# Introduction

Leiden clustering of a cell-cell neighbour graph is a standard step of
single-cell analysis. Most implementations are either sequential or, when
parallel, nondeterministic: the labels change with the number of threads.
`clusterLibreville` is a parallel Leiden whose result depends only on the graph,
the options and the seed. The same seed gives the same labels on a laptop and
on a many-core server.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}

                 repos = c("https://btraven00.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
```

Building from source needs a Rust toolchain (`cargo`, `rustc >= 1.85`).

# Clustering a neighbour graph

The package ships a small real graph: scanpy kNN connectivities of 3000
PBMCs (Hao et al. 2021), as a symmetric sparse matrix.

```{r graph}
library(clusterLibreville)
f <- system.file("extdata", "hao3k.mtx", package = "clusterLibreville")
g <- Matrix::readMM(f)
dim(g)
```

`leiden()` returns one integer label per vertex; community 1 is the largest.

```{r leiden}
labels <- leiden(g, resolution = 1, seed = 0)
table(labels)
modularity(g, labels)
```

The number of threads never changes the result:

```{r threads}
identical(leiden(g, seed = 0, threads = 1), leiden(g, seed = 0, threads = 4))
```

Higher resolutions give more, smaller communities:

```{r resolution}
vapply(c(0.5, 1, 2), function(r) max(leiden(g, resolution = r)), integer(1))
```

# Bioconductor workflows

On a `SingleCellExperiment`, `leiden()` clusters the shared nearest neighbour
graph of a reduced dimension (built by `bluster::makeSNNGraph()`) and returns a
factor, ready for `colLabels()`:

```{r sce}
library(SingleCellExperiment)
set.seed(1)
pcs <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(1000, 0), ncol = 10),
                matrix(rnorm(1000, 3), ncol = 10))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = matrix(0, 5, 200)),
                            reducedDims = list(PCA = pcs))
colLabels(sce) <- leiden(sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 10, seed = 1)
table(colLabels(sce))
```

`cluster_libreville()` has igraph's community-function interface, so it plugs
into bluster's graph-based clustering:

```{r bluster}
param <- bluster::SNNGraphParam(k = 10, cluster.fun = cluster_libreville,
                                cluster.args = list(resolution = 1, seed = 1))
table(bluster::clusterRows(pcs, param))
```

# Options

* `resolution`: the modularity resolution (gamma).
* `seed`: a non-negative whole number; the only source of randomness.
* `n_iterations`: Leiden iterations; `-1` (the default) iterates until an
    iteration changes nothing.
* `theta`: randomness of the refinement step.
* `min_gain`: with `n_iterations = -1`, also stop once an iteration gains less
    modularity than this.
* `threads`: worker threads (default: all cores); does not change the result.
* `details = TRUE`: also return how the run ended (iterations, whether it
  converged, why it stopped, modularity).
